title: A Real-time Execution System of Multimodal Transformer through PIM-GPU Collaboration
problem: Multimodal transformers suffer from high memory consumption and insufficient data reuse, creating severe memory bandwidth bottlenecks that prevent real-time inference.
motivation: Real-time execution of multimodal transformers is critical for practical applications but is severely constrained by memory bandwidth and data reuse limitations.
method: They created a compiler that coordinates work between processing-in-memory units (which compute right where data sits, cutting data movement) and GPUs (which handle math-intensive tasks). At the core is an algorithm that decides optimal data placement and task scheduling for inputs that vary in size. This approach breaks the memory bandwidth bottleneck by reducing how much data needs to travel between storage and processors.
key_novelty: A compiler that splits multimodal transformer work between processing-in-memory units (which reduce data movement) and GPUs (which handle computation), using an algorithm tailored for inputs that vary in size.
contributions: PIM-GPU collaboration compiler framework tailored for multimodal transformers
Specialized PIM allocation algorithm for variable-length input optimization
Compiler-based approach that reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks
Demonstrates 15x end-to-end speedup on multimodal transformer inference
limitations: Specific limitations, ablation studies, and detailed performance breakdowns are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Heterogeneous PIM-GPU compilation for real-time multimodal transformers
